title: cache warmth heatmap + bandwidth runbook
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures an experiment plan, quick runbook, and early observations for generating 'cache warmth' heatmaps and correlating them with memory bandwidth and paging events. The goal is to find actionable signals for smarter async eviction and prefetch thresholds that reduce NVMe paging and DMA stalls without regressing tail latency.

Background / motivation:
- We've observed intermittent throughput drops when long-context chat workloads cause KV residency churn.
- Hypothesis: hotset "islands" and stridey access patterns cause sudden memory-channel saturation and NVMe fallbacks; current LRU-ish eviction is too myopic.
- Need a lightweight visualization + metrics pipeline to relate per-shard reuse distribution to observed DRAM/NIC/PCIe bandwidth and paging counts.

Key jargon used here:
- warmth = recent reuse frequency of KV entries (sliding-window hits per entry)
- hotset island = contiguous set of keys with above-threshold warmth in a time-slice
- spillback/paging = KV spilling to NVMe or remote node due to memory pressure
- async-evict = background eviction thread that demotes entries proactively based on predicted reuse

High-level experiment outline:
1) Instrument runtime to capture per-epoch (1s) samples of: hit counts per KV-key, last-access age distribution, resident_size bytes, total DRAM bandwidth (per NUMA node), PCIe writes, NVMe read/write ops, swap/page-in counts.
2) Aggregate into heatmap tiles: key-bucket by popularity rank (0..1000) vs age bucket (0..60s), produce 2D histogram every 5s.
3) Correlate peaks in DDR bandwidth and NVMe ops with heatmap transitions (appearance of new hot islands or rapid decay in warmth).
4) Run controlled traffic shapes: steady small-context, burst long-context (many distinct tokens), synthetic stridey access (simulate many sessions sampling across long histories) and real logged workloads replayed from prod traces (redacted).

Measurement details / telemetry to collect:
- Per-shard: heatmap (json) for warmth bins, tracked every 5s; keep 1h ring buffer on disk for postmortem.
- Counters: total_hits, total_misses, eviction_count, async_eviction_actions, forced_spillbacks.
- System metrics: perf counters for memory bandwidth (via pcm or perf), NVMe io stats (iostat), PCIe driver stats if available.
- Tracing: add event markers for 'eviction window start/end', 'prefetch launched', 'spillback triggered'.

Visualization plan:
- Heatmap viewer (quick) — tsv-like rows: time, hot_bucket_0..hot_bucket_n, mem_bw, nvme_iops, spillbacks. We can prototype in jq + gnuplot.
- Correlation overlays: show mem_bw curve and NVMe ops on the same timeline as heatmap frames.

Experiment variants (what to run):
A. Baseline: current runtime, default eviction heuristics.
B. Aggressive async-evict: reduce demotion threshold, run eviction sooner (background), keep same batch size.
C. Prefetch-on-hotset: when a hotset island grows, prefetch predicted adjacent keys into local memory (only when mem_bw < threshold).
D. Bandwidth-aware eviction: throttle background evictions when DDR bandwidth > X% to avoid thrashing.
E. KV sharding tweak: temporary increase shard count to evaluate contention impact.

Success metrics / acceptance criteria:
- 99th pct latency no worse than +5% vs baseline under synthetic and replayed traces.
- NVMe write amplification reduced by >20% for long-context burst profile.
- Page-in events reduced or shifted (fewer reactive spillbacks).
- Heatmap reveals stable hotset islands with lower churn in successful configs.

Quick-run commands (local dev box):
- build: bazel build //serving/runtime:kv_agent && bazel build //tools:heatmap-collector
- start: ./bazel-bin/serving/runtime/kv_agent --sample-heatmap --sample-interval=5s --heatmap-output=/tmp/heatmap.log
- capture system stats: sudo perf stat -e mem_load_uops_retired.l1_misses,LLC-load-misses -p $PID -o /tmp/perf.out &
- nvme: iostat -x 1 > /tmp/iostat.log &
- tail merge: jq -s 'flatten' /tmp/heatmap.log > /tmp/heatmap-merged.json

Preliminary observations (from 2025-01-23 internal run, synthetic stridey):
- Hotset islands often form within first 20s of a burst and then migrate; migration correlates with sudden spike in per-NUMA memory BW.
- When BW saturates, async-evict threads observed increased latencies and more forced spillbacks (likely due to eviction machinery competing for memory bandwidth).
- On nodes with PCIe-v4 NVMe, observed lower reactive page-in latency but higher write amplification.
- Simple fixed-threshold async-evict caused oscillation: aggressive mode improved miss-rate but increased NVMe ops and occasionally tail latency.

Hypotheses to validate:
- H1: Eviction should be windowed with momentum-awareness (if a hotset just grew, avoid aggressive eviction elsewhere).
- H2: Memory-bandwidth-aware backoff for eviction threads will reduce NVMe spillbacks without hurting hit-rate much.
- H3: Prefetching nearby keys only when mem BW headroom exists will capture adjacency locality without adding thrash.

Next steps (actionable):
- [Asha] Add per-shard heatmap writer and a compact schema (proto) for 2D bins. (GH PR draft linked below)
- [Miguel] Wire perf counters and NVMe iostat into the existing observability pipeline (log to local tracing stream).
- [Lynn] Prepare 3 replay traces: small-context steady, long-context burst, stridey synthetic. Redact PII.
- Run 3 A/B tests comparing baseline vs bandwidth-aware eviction for 2 hours per trace; collect heatmap + system metrics.

Open questions / risks:
- Overhead: heatmap gathering adds CPU and memory; need to measure collector overhead. Aim <2% CPU for hot path.
- Privacy: storing key-level heatmaps — ensure keys are hashed and non-reversible.
- Sampling granularity tradeoffs: 1s vs 5s buckets — small buckets more accurate but more heavy.

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider instead of per-key, use per-prefix (hash prefixes) to reduce cardinality.
- Use exponential smoothing on warmth to reduce noise from bursty single-session accesses.
- Potential quick win: tune async-evict to use cgroup cpu shares so it cannot starve serving threads.

References / artifacts:
- GH: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/482 (heatmap writer PoC)
- JIRA: INF-732 (KV eviction followups)
- Quick sketch: confluence/cache-ops-heatmap (internal)

Appendix: compact heatmap schema (proto-ish)
- time_ms: string (iso)
- bucket_count: string (int)
- buckets: string (comma separated counts)
- mem_bw_bytes_s: string (int)
- nvme_ops_s: string (int)
- forced_spillbacks: string (int)

(keep this runbook until we have 2 clean A/B runs and a follow-up doc with plots)

-- end of runbook --
